members.name: version
members.says: The API version: 1 while the API is experimental v1.

members.name: getState
members.says: The build: every placed part as a node (and the raw state, which is opaque).

members.name: listProps
members.says: The props library: every prop a build can stage, and which are plants and which are pots.

members.name: listParts
members.says: Every part a script can name: the value, the op and field that take it, its name, what it is for and its printed size.

members.name: openSockets
members.says: Every place one kind of part fits now, each with the exact op that puts it there.

members.name: validate
members.says: Waits for the collision gate, then reports every issue with the build on screen.

members.name: bom
members.says: The parts list, the printed-part count against the download cap, notes, and the print pack link for a bed and format.

members.name: toUrl
members.says: The build as a share-link fragment (v2s=…), without the leading #.

members.name: apply
members.ts: apply(op: HexOp, options?: { readonly dryRun?: boolean }): Promise<MutationOutcome>;
members.says: Apply one op through the same path a click takes; resolves to its outcome. With { dryRun: true } (addProp, moveProp, plant; configurator only), the op is worked out and settled exactly as it would be, and its outcome says what it would add and remove: nothing is written.

members.name: applyAll
members.ts: applyAll(ops: readonly HexOp[], options?: ApplyAllOptions): Promise<BatchResult>;
members.says: Apply ops in order; atomic and stop-on-refusal by default. The ops it applies are one undo step.

members.name: load
members.ts: load(input: string | StarterState): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; code: 'DECODE_FAILED' | 'LINK_TOO_BIG'; message: string }>;
members.says: Replace the build with a share link, or with a starter state of bases.

members.name: undo
members.says: Undo the last change, as Ctrl+Z does. False when there is nothing to undo.

members.name: redo
members.says: Redo, as Ctrl+Shift+Z does. False when there is nothing to redo.

members.name: settle
members.says: Resolves when every model is drawn and the collision gate is idle.

members.name: measure
members.says: The build's size as drawn, mm (height is y): the parts alone and with its props, each a box with its min, max and size; null when empty (configurator only).

members.name: surfaces
members.ts: surfaces(ref?: NodeRef, options?: { readonly fits?: string }): Promise<readonly Surface[]>;
members.says: Where a prop can go on or in one part, or every part with no ref: its tops, floors, compartments and soil, each with its outline and headroom; with { fits: <prop id> }, only those a prop of that size could take lying on its shortest side (a first cut: the dry run is the answer). Pass one to addProp as surface (configurator only).

ops.says: Place a prop from listProps() on a part, a placed prop or the bench, resting as the props panel rests it (configurator only). Refused for where or how it rests (PROP_NO_REST, PROP_WOULD_SHIFT), details.tryInstead may hold the same op varied (its other pose, a turn, a small shift) that does place: send it as it is.

fields.name: id
fields.says: A prop from listProps().

fields.name: on
fields.says: What it stands on: a piece, cover, cap, bin, drawer or soil part, a placed prop, or the bench; or a spool axle (axle:...), which a filament spool HANGS on, with no aim; a surface id from surfaces() is taken as that surface. Left out: whatever is under the aim.

fields.name: atMm
fields.type: { readonly x: number; readonly z: number }
fields.says: Aim straight down at this point, mm. Left out: the centre of on; for the bench, clear of the build.

fields.name: yawDeg
fields.says: A turn about the vertical, degrees.

fields.name: pose
fields.says: 'rest': its resting pose (addProp always rests it; moveProp keeps the prop's own turn unless this is 'rest'). 'stand' or 'lie': the prop's authored pose (a screwdriver stands handle up, a mug stands mouth up, a plate lies on its foot), set whole and only verified by a drop: refused PROP_WOULD_SHIFT if it would move more than 15 mm or turn more than 10 degrees. A prop with no authored poses, or not that one, is refused INVALID_INPUT naming the poses it takes.

fields.name: facingDeg
fields.says: With pose 'stand' or 'lie': the bearing its front points (a mug's handle, a laptop's keyboard side, a book's spine), or for a prop with no front its long side when that lies level (a screwdriver laid along a slot), degrees about up from +x as yawDeg turns. Left out: yawDeg.

fields.name: drop
fields.says: Let it fall and settle, as the props panel's Drop does.

fields.name: surface
fields.says: A surface from surfaces(): aimed at its centre (or at atMm inside it) from just over it, so nothing above it is met first. Instead of on (configurator only).

fields.name: orient
fields.type: { readonly up?: 'natural' | 'long' | 'short'; readonly longAlong?: 'x' | 'z' | number; readonly flip?: boolean }
fields.says: Turned by intent, from the prop's own size: up 'long' stands it on end, 'short' lays it flat, 'natural' (the default) keeps its rest; longAlong lays its longest level side along x, z or a bearing (degrees about up from +x, as yawDeg turns); flip turns it end over end (a screwdriver modelled handle down stands handle up). yawDeg turns it after.

refusals.says: That part is already fitted here.
This cell holds a bin whose rim is in the joint the part needs.
A bin below has its rim in the joint a stacking collar needs.
A bolt-on under this cell comes up where the part would sit.
A port's bore would be closed by an accessory plate.
The props panel is mid-action (a prop in hand, a settle or a soil fill): try again when it is done (browser only).
An edge cap closes the face this part would butt against.
There is no cell at that position.
A stacking collar is in the joint the bin rim needs.
A cut joint needs two halves facing each other across the cut.
The input is not a hex build link (v2s= or v2u=), or it carries more than 20,000 parts.
The recess or face already holds something.
A part on a neighbouring cell reaches into this position.
The flat already carries a part.
A footprint already covers this cell top.
The bin is cut to a different cell outline.
The joint needs the other gender (male or female) here.
That part of the cell already holds a bin.
The notch takes the other hand here.
The other half of the cell holds a part this one cannot share with.
The build changed under the op: while it worked out its answer (nothing was written), or after it wrote, when the collision gate put back an earlier part or the user edited (browser only).
The op is malformed: a missing field, a wrong type, an unknown op.
The part name is not one the configurator places.
A base carries only its own kind: the cell below is a different shape.
The part below is lidded; the lid must come off before anything stands on it.
Only a bolt-type cover carries the accessory bolt pattern.
The op, or the starter state given to load(), would take the build past 20,000 parts, more than a link can carry.
Something stands on this part; take that off first.
The rules allow it but the geometry does not: the collision gate put the build back (browser only).
The op needs the drawn build: run it in the configurator (window.hexAPI), not headless.
The part hangs through stories below and needs a tall base.
No node matches that ref.
The two cells do not share a flat.
There is no notch or bay drawer at that corner.
The prop is not a plant that goes in soil.
The prop is not a pot.
The part is not a notch or bay part.
The part seats in full hexes only.
One side has no whole rectangle of four bolt holes.
There is no side bore on this flat.
There is no cell here to fit the part to.
There is nothing across this flat to bolt to.
The op would change nothing.
There is nothing to build on here.
A spool axle needs a rod socket facing this one across an empty cell.
The part holds no soil yet: fillSoil first.
A cell is outside |q|, |r| <= 256 or 0 <= level <= 63.
The part would reach into a neighbouring space: the position across a flat, or the quarters a long or open drawer reaches.
The part is withheld from the current release.
A pipe runs across the flat where the part would bolt.
A pipe runs through the side bores where the bin would hang; a third-depth bin clears a plain pipe, not a coupling or fitting.
The pot holds no soil yet.
The pot already holds a plant.
A placed prop already has exactly that pose: the op would make a twin (browser only).
No placed prop has that ref.

Nothing under the aim gives the prop a place to rest, or it would run into something; the message says which, and details.obstacle names what it runs into (a node ref, prop:<entry>, or null for the bench or soil) and details.depthMm how far it would sit inside it, when known (browser only).
The prop id is not in the props library (listProps).

Posed 'stand' or 'lie', the prop would not stay: the drop that verifies it moves it more than 15 mm or turns it more than 10 degrees (it would fall into the bin, tip over); details.movedMm and details.turnedDeg say how far (browser only).
A port on a neighbouring cell points into this position.
The pipe has no axis to run along here.
A bin hangs through the side bores the pipe needs; a third-depth bin clears a plain pipe, not a coupling or fitting.
A part already fills a cell the pipe would pass through.
The cover hub has no clearance here.
The cover hub has nothing to mount to.
The cover hub is a provisional fitting.
A part is bolted over the flat the pipe needs.
The bend needs a flexible section that is not allowed here.
Runs plumbed for different duties meet.
The pipe must enter or leave through a cell boundary.
No path through the given cells.
The pipe changes storey without a riser.
The run needs a fitting that is still provisional.
A riser stands under a cover that would close it.
Too many pipes meet at one socket.
The socket the pipe was cut to is gone.
More arms meet at one fitting than any fitting takes.
A pipe run already puts a connector here.
The flat is a seam against another cell, not an outside face.
Another part already fills that position.
The part does not bolt to that slot.
The cell has no room for the part.
A pipe socket on the lid would be lifted by a bin rim.
The part cannot hold soil: soil goes in a bin, a bolt-on bin, or a notch or bay bin.
No soil bed could be cut for the part (browser only).
The part has no dividers to fill to: fill it to the rim.
A spike on the junction reaches into this position, or a spike and a drawer would share a corner of a cell.
Inserts cannot be stacked in this order here.
Too many stories: bases go 1-3, caps 1-2, drawers 1-3.
A two-story cap needs the same face on both stories.
The op did not finish working out its answer in time and wrote nothing (browser only).
A spike sits where three cells meet, and one is missing.
A handle needs all three recesses of its triangle under covers.
That type does not fit here, or the part does not turn by that step.
Nothing below carries the part.
The cell top is a wedged socket cover a bin rim would lift.
A pipe runs through this part or face, and the change would break it.

issues.says: error: a base is not held up.
error: a part has lost what held it.
error: a pipe run is not legal where it stands.
warning: parts could slide apart; joint bolts lock them.
warning: more printed parts than one download takes (bom().maxPackInstances).
warning: the build names a part that is not in the current release.
info: faces that could take an edge cap. They are listed in the message only, for people; ask openSockets for the cap sites.
warning (apply only): the op is in, and the build still holds a clash it already had (a link that arrived overlapping); validate().meshClash names it.
warning (apply only): the collision gate did not judge the op in time; it may still be put back.
warning (validate): a placed prop would still drop more than 3 mm: it rests on nothing.
warning (validate): a placed prop is inside a part or another prop.
warning (validate): a plug plant stands in no soil.

types.name: Cell
types.says: An axial cell (q, r) and its storey (level, 0 at the ground).

types.name: Site
types.says: A cell with no storey, as edges and junctions name them.

types.name: Face
types.says: A face of a cell.

types.name: Variant
types.says: A cell shape: full, a half or a quarter.

types.name: NodeFamily
types.says: The kind of a node. Other families may appear while the API is experimental.

types.name: NodeRef
types.says: An opaque handle for one placed part: read it, pass it back, never build one.

types.name: PropRef
types.says: An opaque handle for one placed prop: read it, pass it back, never build one. It changes when the prop does (moved, or a pot filled or planted), and the outcome names the new one.

types.name: HexNode
types.says: One placed part.

types.name: StarterState
types.says: A build of bases and snaps only, for load().

types.name: PartInfo
types.says: One part a script can name, as listParts() gives it.

types.name: PropInfo
types.says: One prop of the library, as listProps() gives it.

types.name: Staging
types.says: The props on the build and the soil in its parts: staging, not parts, so not in nodes or the BOM. Positions are mm, y up.

types.name: HexState
types.says: What getState() returns.

types.name: HexOp
types.says: One change to the build. The op field names it.

types.name: SocketQuery
types.says: What openSockets() looks for.

types.name: BoxMm
types.says: A box in world mm, y up (x and z across the bench).

types.name: Measure
types.says: What measure() returns: the build's box, the parts alone and with its props; null for an empty build.

types.name: Surface
types.says: One place on or in a part a prop can go: a top, a floor, one compartment of a divided bin, or a soil seat; or a deck of flush neighbouring tops. Lengths are mm, y up.

types.name: OpenSocket
types.says: One place a part fits now.

types.name: RefusalCode
types.says: Why an op was refused. Branch on it; new codes may appear while the API is experimental.

types.name: IssueCode
types.says: What validate() found.

types.name: Issue
types.says: One finding.

types.name: MeshClash
types.says: The collision gate's verdict: clear, not run, or the two parts that collide and by how much (mm).

types.name: ValidationReport
types.says: What validate() returns.

types.name: MutationOutcome
types.says: The answer to every op: what changed, or which rule said no.

types.name: ApplyAllOptions
types.says: How applyAll() treats a refusal.

types.name: BatchResult
types.says: What applyAll() returns.

types.name: BomLine
types.says: One line of the parts list.

types.name: BomSummary
types.says: What bom() returns.

types.name: PackOptions
types.says: The print pack bom() links to.

types.name: PackLink
types.says: The print pack for a build: the link, the bed and format it is for, or why there is none.
